summary.intent: Wrap up the Callisto spec/refactor/dependency PRs, then decide whether and how to build OIDC trusted publishing support, researching it first and avoiding over-engineering.
summary.outcome: PRs #554-#557 were merged (spec hygiene, one target-triple table, simulator using Dag::descendants, michi-graph 0.10 bump). Research on OIDC showed Callisto needs almost no code, so the user chose to defer it and the findings were recorded in NEXT-WORK.md without any PRs, code or trail.

repo: Callisto follows ADR 4: authentication stays with the ecosystem tool, with no credential pre-flight. A missing credential surfaces only as the tool's own failure, reported as E163.
docs/stability.md says a new callisto.toml key or action input becomes permanent API, so OIDC should add neither.
Generated workflows already give `execute` `id-token: write`. Callisto's own release policy check allows `id-token` only on build-artifact.
Template changes require updating pinned snapshot files (init tests `..._bytes_are_pinned`) and the 'no secret outside execute' assertions.
Callisto's own workflow keeps `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as the one registry secret in `execute`.

The `callisto-graph` test `a_version_the_registry_serves_is_exact_with_no_checksum_or_yank_claim` runs real `cargo info` against a local registry. It is likely the intermittent exit 101 seen on local runs, and CI installs the registry tools so it should be unaffected (unproven).

code.finding: The temp npm config is written only if NPM_TOKEN is non-empty. It copies the user's .npmrc and appends an `_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}` line. With no token there is no _authToken line, so npm's OIDC fallback is not blocked.

`credentials_needed_by()` keeps ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_* only for npm/pnpm/yarn/bun and strips it, TWINE_* and PYPI_TOKEN from other children including cargo and twine. The draft doc's claim that Callisto never strips them is wrong for twine and cargo.
An empty NPM_TOKEN is filtered to None, so the npm publisher env is empty.
Build backends have their credentials stripped in the same way as runner.rs.
`ALLOWED_WRITES["execute"]={"contents"}` rejects `id-token: write` on execute. EXECUTE_SECRETS (line 24, 61) can become empty and the check still passes.

workflow: Use parallel read-only research agents for design questions, and verify key subagent claims directly (for example runner.rs:82-97) before relying on them.
Subagent reports are not user authority. Treat them as evidence only, and flag unverified claims such as inferences and issue-tracker reports.
Challenging scope with 'are we over-engineering?' before building shrank a six-item feature to docs plus a possible tiny change. Check whether the existing tools already do the work.
Keep a NEXT-WORK.md plan that records deferred decisions and research so they are not re-derived.

friction: The draft OIDC design doc contained unverified or wrong claims that needed research to correct: the 'never strips' claim and the unverified empty-token npm behaviour.

Real OIDC behaviour (empty _authToken blocking, composite-action matching, twine needing TWINE_USERNAME=__token__, crates.io against non-default registries) cannot be verified without owner-run scratch packages on real registries.
Package-manager OIDC support is poorly documented or broken: pnpm 11.0.8 regressed with a 404, yarn berry has no docs, and bun has an open issue.
npm's trusted-publisher mismatch surfaces as a misleading E404.
The working tree has many stray scratch files (.tmp, .probe, .p.pl, zz_scratch_exit_kind.rs) listed among modified files.
open_items: OIDC trusted publishing is deferred. If revived: an npm docs note (leave NPM_TOKEN unset, omit registry-url and NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, keep .npmrc free of _authToken lines) plus a fake-registry no-token test; allow twine to keep the OIDC vars; a crates.io auth-action step in the generated workflow.
Owner decision: whether Callisto's own `execute` job may hold `id-token: write`, which would let it drop CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN.
michi: configure the npm trusted publisher and unset NPM_TOKEN if the org token deprecation is still a deadline.
Delete the stale remote branch origin/fix/version-lock-refresh-rollback.
Enable the GitHub immutable releases setting, currently off.
Decide whether root-level npm pins should error or be documented.
Close or revive stale draft PR #495.
Optional E163 hint for npm's misleading E404 would add new error text and needs owner confirmation.
Clean up stray scratch files in the working tree.
